topic.title: In May 2010 Laszlo Hanyecz paid 10,000 bitcoin for two Papa John's pizzas; on Pizza Day 2026 those coins were worth more than $767 million

title: Laszlo Hanyecz paid bitcoin for two pizzas. What did they cost him? 🍕
description:
In May 2010, Laszlo Hanyecz paid for two Papa John's pizzas with bitcoin. What did those pizzas really cost him?
A true story of one purchase, not a tip: nobody here says what bitcoin will do next.
Sources: Cointelegraph (May 2026). The characters are not advisers.
Illustrative only. Not financial advice.

cta: The pizza or the coins: which would you have kept? Comment

lines.text: Laszlo Hanyecz paid for 2 pizzas with bitcoin. So what did they really cost him?
He paid 10,000 coins, the first real purchase ever made with bitcoin.
Back then, all those coins were worth about $41.
That's about $20 a pizza. A fair deal?
Bitcoin soared, crashed and soared again. So what were those coins worth later?
On Pizza Day this year, the same coins were worth more than $767M.
Pizza or coins: which would you keep? He chose pizza.

Beat 'climb': 'Then bitcoin's price kept climbing, year after year.' is false and misleading: bitcoin fell in several calendar years (about -56% in 2014, -73% in 2018, -64% in 2022), and the line presents bitcoin as a steady riser, which the topic's verify list forbids ('never present bitcoin as an investment'). Suggested fix: 'Bitcoin's price then soared, with big crashes along the way. So what were those coins worth later?'

Hook and loop pictures (fix while rewriting climb): the moments show Laszlo paying the Papa John's driver from his laptop ('hands over nothing but points at his laptop', 'the driver arrives again'). He actually posted an offer online and paid 10,000 BTC to another person, who had the pizzas delivered (Cointelegraph: 'posted an online offer'). Show the payment going to a forum stranger on screen, not the driver.

Facts confirmed on the Cointelegraph source page (22 May 2026): 10,000 BTC, two Papa John's pizzas, about $41 then, more than $767 million on Pizza Day 2026, the 'first recorded commercial Bitcoin transaction'. 'On Pizza Day this year' holds only while the video is published in 2026; the disclaimer ends the description.
